- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high or adjust downward by 3–5% after 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (avg > 0.2) but model forecasts decline, reduce forecast slope by 15–20% to avoid overreacting to sentiment.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish; add 2–3% upward bias to forecast mid-range.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead by 1–2% to align with sentiment momentum.
- If recent 18-day history shows strong downward trend + negative sentiment, model often fails to recognize continuation; apply 3–5% downward bias to 30d forecast.
